put.summary: Open an existing project-space in the background and return the job that is doing it
put.description:
Open an existing project-space in the background and return the job that is doing it.

Opening a project written by an older SIRIUS converts it first, which on a large project takes minutes. This endpoint returns as soon as the project id is reserved, so a client can show what is happening and stay responsive; the project becomes usable when the job reaches DONE, announced by a PROJECT_OPENED event as well. The synchronous variant is unchanged and still available.

Cancelling the job is safe: a conversion fills in only what a record is missing and records the schema version last, so an interrupted one leaves the project as it was and simply runs again next time.

post.summary: Create a new, empty custom database
post.description:
Create a new, empty custom database.

The new database is created on disk and registered with this SIRIUS instance, so it can immediately be used as a search parameter and imported into via the import endpoint. It contains no structures and no reference spectra until something is imported.

parameters.name: databaseId
parameters.description:
id of the new database. Must be URL-safe, that is letters, digits, '-' and '_' only,
                    and must not be in use by another database.

requestBody.description:
optional settings for the new database. If omitted, the database is created in the
                    default custom database directory with default settings. Supply a location to place
                    the database file elsewhere, a displayName for the user interface, and
                    matchRtOfReferenceSpectra for in-house libraries whose retention times are comparable
                    to the measured samples.

500.description: Unexpected server-side error. The problem detail carries the reason.

400.description: The database id is not a valid database name. It must consist of letters, digits, '-' and '_' only.

409.description: A database with this id already exists, or a file already exists at the target location.

get.summary: Get runs in the given project-space
get.description:
Get runs in the given project-space.

Supported filter syntax

The filter string must contain one or more clauses. A clause is prefixed by a field name.

Searchable fields are the indexed properties of the run (e.g. name, source, chromatography, ionization) and project tags prefixed with the namespace tags. (e.g. tags.MyTag). Use the searchable-fields endpoint (getRunsSearchableFields) to list all fields that can be searched, including their value type, whether they support word based (full text) search, and whether results can be sorted by them. Possible value types are text, integer, double, boolean, date, or time.

The format of the date type is yyyy-MM-dd and of the time type is HH\:mm\:ss.

A clause may be:

  • a term: field name followed by a colon and the search term, e.g. chromatography:LC
  • a phrase: field name followed by a colon and the search phrase in doublequotes, e.g. name:"Blank Sample 25"
  • a regular expression: field name followed by a colon and the regex in slashes, e.g. tags.MyTagA:/[mb]oat/
  • a comparison: field name followed by a comparison operator and a value, e.g. tags.MyTagB<3
  • a range: field name followed by a colon and an open (indiced by [ and ] ) or (semi-)closed range (indiced by { and }), e.g. tags.MyTagB:[* TO 3]

Clauses may be grouped with brackets ( and ) and / or joined with AND or OR (or && and || )

Example

The syntax allows to build complex filter queries such as:

name:"Blank" AND chromatography:LC AND tags.city:"new york" OR tags.MyDateTag:[2023-10-01 TO 2023-12-24] OR tags.time<10\:00\:00

get.summary: Page of available compounds (group of ion identities) in the given project-space
get.description:
Page of available compounds (group of ion identities) in the given project-space.

Supported filter syntax

The filter string must contain one or more clauses. A clause is prefixed by a field name.

Use the searchable-fields endpoint (getCompoundsSearchableFields) to list the fields that can be searched - since compound-level indexing is not implemented yet, it currently returns an empty list (nothing searchable). The syntax below describes how queries will work once compound search is supported; tag based fields are prefixed with the namespace tags.. Possible value types are text, integer, double, boolean, date, or time.

The format of the date type is yyyy-MM-dd and of the time type is HH\:mm\:ss.

A clause may be:

  • a term: field name followed by a colon and the search term, e.g. tags.MyTagA:sample
  • a phrase: field name followed by a colon and the search phrase in doublequotes, e.g. tags.MyTagA:"Some Text"
  • a regular expression: field name followed by a colon and the regex in slashes, e.g. tags.MyTagA:/[mb]oat/
  • a comparison: field name followed by a comparison operator and a value, e.g. tags.MyTagB<3
  • a range: field name followed by a colon and an open (indiced by [ and ] ) or (semi-)closed range (indiced by { and }), e.g. tags.MyTagB:[* TO 3]

Clauses may be grouped with brackets ( and ) and / or joined with AND or OR (or && and || )

Example

The syntax allows to build complex filter queries such as:

tags.city:"new york" AND tags.ATextTag:/[mb]oat/ AND tags.count:[1 TO *] OR tags.realNumberTag<=3.2 OR tags.MyDateTag:2024-01-01 OR tags.MyDateTag:[2023-10-01 TO 2023-12-24] OR tags.MyDateTag<2022-01-01 OR tags.time:12\:00\:00 OR tags.time:[12\:00\:00 TO 14\:00\:00] OR tags.time<10\:00\:00

Note: compound-level indexing is not implemented yet, so this endpoint always reads from the project database. Passing a non-empty searchQuery is therefore not supported and responds with 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED. Omit the parameter to page over all compounds.

get.summary: Get features (aligned over runs) in the given project-space
get.description:
Get features (aligned over runs) in the given project-space.

Supported filter syntax

The filter string must contain one or more clauses. A clause is prefixed by a field name.

Searchable fields are the indexed properties of the feature (e.g. ionMass, name, quality, hasMsMs), its annotations addressed via dot notation (e.g. topAnnotations.structureAnnotation.structureName), and project tags prefixed with the namespace tags. (e.g. tags.MyTag). Use the searchable-fields endpoint (getAlignedFeaturesSearchableFields) to list all fields that can be searched, including their value type, whether they support word based (full text) search, and whether results can be sorted by them. Possible value types are text, integer, double, boolean, date, or time.

The format of the date type is yyyy-MM-dd and of the time type is HH\:mm\:ss.

A clause may be:

  • a term: field name followed by a colon and the search term, e.g. tags.MyTagA:sample
  • a phrase: field name followed by a colon and the search phrase in doublequotes, e.g. name:"Bicuculline methiodide"
  • a regular expression: field name followed by a colon and the regex in slashes, e.g. tags.MyTagA:/[mb]oat/
  • a comparison: field name followed by a comparison operator and a value, e.g. ionMass<300
  • a range: field name followed by a colon and an open (indiced by [ and ] ) or (semi-)closed range (indiced by { and }), e.g. ionMass:[300 TO 400]
  • a boolean: boolean fields are matched as follows: e.g. hasMsMs:true, tags.MyTagA:false
  • a value-less: tags without values (See TagDefinition) are matched as follows: e.g. tags.MyTagA:* or tags.MyTagA:true

Clauses may be grouped with brackets ( and ) and / or joined with AND or OR (or && and || )

Example

The syntax allows to build complex filter queries such as:

ionMass:[300 TO 400] AND quality:GOOD AND topAnnotations.compoundClassAnnotation.npcPathway:"Alkaloids" AND tags.city:"new york" OR tags.MyDateTag:[2023-10-01 TO 2023-12-24] OR tags.time<10\:00\:00

SCORE: Use them for SCORING. To use this the instrument should produce clear MS/MS isotope patterns

IGNORE: Ignore that there might be isotope patterns in MS/MS

filterByIsotopePattern.description: When filtering is enabled, molecular formulas are excluded if their theoretical isotope pattern does not match the measured one, even if their MS/MS pattern has high score.

enforceElGordoFormula.description: El Gordo may predict that an MS/MS spectrum is a lipid spectrum. If enabled, the corresponding molecular formula will be enforced as a molecular formula candidate.

performBottomUpSearch.description: If true, molecular formula generation via bottom up search is enabled.

performDenovoBelowMz.description: Specifies the m/z below which de novo molecular formula generation is enabled. Set to 0 to disable de novo molecular formula generation.

formulaSearchDBs.description:
List of structure databases to extract molecular formulas from, to reduce the formula search space.
 SIRIUS is quite good at de novo formula annotation, so only enable if you have a good reason.

applyFormulaConstraintsToDBAndBottomUpSe.description:
By default, the formula (element) constraints are only applied to de novo molecular formula generation.
 If true, the constraints are as well applied to database search and bottom up search.

enforcedFormulaConstraints.description:
These configurations hold the information how to autodetect elements based on the given formula constraints. Note: If the compound is already assigned to a specific molecular formula, this annotation is ignored.

Enforced: Enforced elements are always considered

fallbackFormulaConstraints.description:
These configurations hold the information how to autodetect elements based on the given formula constraints. Note: If the compound is already assigned to a specific molecular formula, this annotation is ignored.

Fallback: Fallback elements are used, if the auto-detection fails (e.g. no isotope pattern available)

detectableElements.description:
These configurations hold the information how to autodetect elements based on the given formula constraints. Note: If the compound is already assigned to a specific molecular formula, this annotation is ignored.

Detectable: Detectable elements are added to the chemical alphabet, if there are indications for them (e.g. in isotope pattern)

injectSpecLibMatchFormulas.description:
If true formula candidates that belong to spectral library matches above a certain threshold will
 be injected and preserved for further analyses, no matter which score they have or which filter is applied

minScoreToInjectSpecLibMatch.description:
Similarity Threshold to inject formula candidates no matter which score/rank they have or which filter settings are applied.
 If the threshold is >= 0, formula candidates with a reference spectrum similarity above the threshold will be injected.

minPeaksToInjectSpecLibMatch.description: Matching peaks threshold to inject formula candidates no matter which score they have or which filter is applied.

Sirius.description:
User/developer friendly parameter subset for the Formula/SIRIUS tool
 Can use results from Spectral library search tool.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the tool is enabled.

spectraSearchDBs.description:
Structure Databases with Reference spectra to search in.

Defaults to BIO + Custom Databases. Possible values are available via the Database API.

precursorDeviationPpm.description: Maximum allowed mass deviation in ppm for matching the precursor. If not specified, the same value as for the peaks is used.

minSimilarity.description: Minimal spectral similarity of a spectral match to be considered a hit.

minNumOfPeaks.description: Minimal number of matching peaks of a spectral match to be considered a hit.

enableAnalogueSearch.description: Enable analogue search in addition to the identity spectral library search

minSimilarityAnalogue.description: Minimal spectral similarity of a spectral match to be considered an analogue hit.

minNumOfPeaksAnalogue.description: Minimal number of matching peaks of a spectral match to be considered an analogue hit.

scoring.description:
NO LONGER SUPPORTED (IGNORED)
 Specify scoring method to match spectra
 INTENSITY: Intensity weighted. Each peak matches at most one peak in the other spectrum.
 GAUSSIAN: Treat peaks as (un-normalized) Gaussians and score overlapping areas of PDFs. Each peak might score against multiple peaks in the other spectrum.
 MODIFIED_COSINE: This algorithm requires that there is at most one pair of peaks (u,v) where the m/z of u and v are within the allowed mass tolerance. To be used for analog search with different precursor masses.

peakDeviationPpm.description:
NO LONGER SUPPORTED (IGNORED)
 Maximum allowed mass deviation in ppm for matching peaks.

SpectralLibrarySearch.description: User/developer friendly parameter subset for the Spectral library search tool.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the tool is enabled.

structureSearchDBs.description:
Structure databases to search in, If expansive search is enabled this DB selection will be expanded to PubChem if no high confidence hit was found in the selected databases.

Defaults to BIO + Custom Databases. Possible values are available via the Database API.

tagStructuresWithLipidClass.description:
Candidates matching the lipid class estimated by El Gordo will be tagged.
 The lipid class will only be available if El Gordo predicts that the MS/MS is a lipid spectrum.
 If this parameter is set to 'false' El Gordo will still be executed and e.g. improve the fragmentation
 tree, but the matching structure candidates will not be tagged if they match lipid class.

expansiveSearchConfidenceMode.description:
Expansive search mode. Expansive search will expand the search space to whole PubChem in case no hit with reasonable confidence was found in one of the specified databases (structureSearchDBs).

Possible Values OFF - No expansive search is performed EXACT - Use confidence score in exact mode: Only molecular structures identical to the true structure should count as correct identification. APPROXIMATE - Use confidence score in approximate mode: Molecular structures hits that are close to the true structure should count as correct identification.

StructureDbSearch.description:
User/developer friendly parameter subset for the CSI:FingerID structure db search tool.
 Needs results from the FingerprintPrediction and CANOPUS tools.
 Non-null parameters in this object override their equivalent value in the config map.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the tool is enabled.

consideredCandidatesAt300Mz.description: Maximum number of candidate molecular formulas (fragmentation trees computed by SIRIUS) per compound which are considered by ZODIAC for compounds below 300 m/z.

consideredCandidatesAt800Mz.description: Maximum number of candidate molecular formulas (fragmentation trees computed by SIRIUS) per compound which are considered by ZODIAC for compounds above 800 m/z.

runInTwoSteps.description: By default, ZODIAC runs a 2-step approach: first running only 'good quality compounds', and afterwards including the remaining ones.

Zodiac.description:
User/developer friendly parameter subset for the ZODIAC tool (network-based molecular formula re-ranking).
 Needs results from the Formula/SIRIUS tool.

compoundIds.description:
Compounds that should be the input for this Job
 Will be converted to the respective alignedFeatureIds for computation.

 At least one compoundId or alignedFeatureId needs to be specified.

alignedFeatureIds.description:
Features (aligned over runs) that should be the input for this Job

 At least one compoundId or alignedFeatureId needs to be specified.

affectedCompoundIds.description: List of compoundIds that have been imported.

affectedAlignedFeatureIds.description: List of alignedFeatureIds that have been imported.

sampleNames.description:
Sample names for each input file to link imported results, e.g. QuantTable back to the input data. If NULL or empty sample names will be derived from the input files.

The names are matched to the input files by index. Partial lists are allowed: a NULL entry and any input file without a corresponding entry get their name derived from the input file. Surplus entries that match no input file are ignored.

Names must neither be blank nor duplicated, otherwise the import is rejected.

sampleTypes.description:
Sample type for each input file to be used to compute fold changes between blank and sample runs If NULL or empty no fold changes will be computed during preprocessing.

The types are matched to the input files by index. In contrast to sampleNames either all or no sample types have to be given: if the number of types does not match the number of input files or if any type is NULL or blank, the import is rejected.

alignLCMSRuns.description: Specifies whether LC/MS runs should be aligned

noiseIntensity.description:
Noise level under which all peaks are considered to be likely noise. A peak has to be at least 3x noise level
 to be picked as feature. Peaks with MS/MS are still picked even though they might be below noise level.
 If not specified, the noise intensity is detected automatically from the data. We recommend NOT specifying
 this parameter, as the automated detection is usually sufficient.

alignMaxRetentionTimeDeviation.description: Maximum allowed retention time error in seconds for aligning features. If not specified, this parameter is estimated from the data.

minSNR.description: Minimum ratio between peak height and noise intensity for detecting features. By default, this value is 3. Features with good MS/MS are always picked independent of their intensity. For picking very low intensity features we recommend a min-snr of 2, but this will increase runtime and storage requirements

luceneQuery.description: Query used to group the entities in lucene format.

features.description: The features this compound consists of.

externalFeatureId.description: Externally provided FeatureId (by some preprocessing tool). This FeatureId is NOT used by SIRIUS but is stored to ease mapping information back to the source.

detectedAdducts.description: Detected adducts of this feature. Can be NULL or empty if no adducts are known.

dataQuality.description: A optional feature quality flag that can be used to filter features to be shown in the gui or to be considered for further analysis.

ms1Spectra.description:
List of MS1Spectra belonging to this feature. These spectra will be merged and only a representative
 mergedMs1 spectrum will be stored in SIRIUS. At least one of these spectra should contain the
 isotope pattern of the precursor ion.
 Note: Will be ignored if 'mergedMs1' is given.

ms2Spectra.description: List of MS/MS spectra that belong to this feature.

FeatureImport.description:
Represents an (aligned) feature to be imported into a SIRIUS project.
 At least one of the Mass Spec data sources (e.g. mergedMs1, ms1Spectra, ms2Spectra) needs to be given.
 Otherwise, the import will fail.

externalFeatureId.description:
Externally provided FeatureId (e.g. by some preprocessing tool).
 This FeatureId is NOT used by SIRIUS but is stored to ease mapping information back to the source.

charge.description: Ion mode (charge) this feature has been measured in.

detectedAdducts.description:
Adducts of this feature that have been detected during preprocessing.
 Never empty: if no adduct could be detected, the unknown ion type matching the feature's
 charge ([M+?]+ or [M+?]-) is reported instead, so every feature is filterable by adduct.

quality.description:
Overall Quality of this feature.
 If no Quality data are available for this feature the value is NOT_APPLICABLE

hasMs1.description: If true, the feature has at least one MS1 spectrum

hasMsMs.description: If true, the feature has at least one MS/MS spectrum

computing.description:
Write lock for this feature. If the feature is locked no write operations are possible.
 True if any computation is modifying this feature or its results

qualities.description: Qualities per top level quality category.

AlignedFeature.description:
The AlignedFeature contains the ID of a feature (aligned over runs) together with some read-only information
 that might be displayed in some summary view.

name.description: Optional display name of this spectrum.

msLevel.description:
MS level of the measured spectrum.
 Artificial spectra with no msLevel (e.g. Simulated Isotope patterns) use null or zero

collisionEnergy.description:
Collision energy used for MS/MS spectra
 Null for spectra where collision energy is not applicable

precursorMz.description:
Precursor m/z of the MS/MS spectrum
 Null for spectra where precursor m/z is not applicable

scanNumber.description:
Scan number of the spectrum.
 Might be null for artificial spectra with no scan number (e.g. Simulated Isotope patterns or merged spectra)

cosineQuery.description:
True if spectrum is in cosine query normalized format.
 Such spectrum is compatible with SpectralLibraryMatch peak assignments to reference spectra.

peaks.description: The peaks of this spectrum which might contain additional annotations such as molecular formulas.

absIntensityFactor.description:
Factor to convert relative intensities to absolute intensities. Might be null or 1 for spectra where absolute intensities are not available (e.g. artificial or merged spectra)

DEPRECATED: Spectra are always returned with raw intensities. Use provided normalization factors to normalize on the fly.

maxNormFactor.description: Factor to convert absolute intensities to MAX norm.

sumNormFactor.description: Factor to convert absolute intensities to SUM norm.

l2NormFactor.description: Factor to convert absolute intensities to L2 (Euclidean) norm.

firstPeakNormFactor.description: Factor to convert absolute intensities to normalize intensities by first peak intensity.

AnnotatedSpectrum.description:
Spectrum model with peak annotations based on the fragmentation tree and Epimetheus substructure annotations.
 Molecular formula and adduct of the spectrum are identical to the ones of the corresponding molecular formula candidate and FragmentationTree.
 Fragment molecular formulas and adducts correspond to the FragmentationTree's FragmentNodes

CanopusPrediction.description:
Container class that holds the CANOPUS compound class predictions for all predictable compound classes.
 This is the full CANOPUS result.

compoundId.description: Unique id of this compound entity.

rtStartSeconds.description: The merged/consensus retention time start (earliest rt) of this compound

rtEndSeconds.description: The merged/consensus retention time end (latest rt) of this compound

neutralMass.description:
Neutral mass of this compound. Ion mass minus the mass of the assigned adduct of each feature of
 this compound should result in the same neutral mass

features.description: List of aligned features (adducts) that belong to the same (this) compound

type.description: Specifies the classification ontology the CompoundClass belongs to.

level.description: Name of the level this compound class belongs to

levelIndex.description: Index of the level this compound class belongs to

id.description: Unique id of the class. Might be undefined for certain classification ontologies.

index.description: Absolute index of this property in the predicted vector/embedding

parentId.description: Unique id of the parent class. Might be undefined for certain classification ontologies.

parentName.description: Name of the parent compound class.

CompoundClass.description:
Predicted compound class with name, probability and id if available.
 (ClassyFire and NPC). This can be seen as the set of classes a feature most likely belongs to

classyFireLineage.description:
Most likely ClassyFire lineage, ordered from least specific to most specific class
 classyFireLineage.get(classyFireLineage.size() - 1) gives the most specific ClassyFire compound class annotation

classyFireAlternatives.description: Alternative ClassyFire classes with high probability that do not fit into the lineage

CompoundClasses.description:
Container class that holds the most likely compound class for different levels of each ontology for a
 certain Compound/Feature/FormulaCandidate/PredictedFingerprint.

ComputedSubtools.description: Specifies which tools have been executed for this feature. Can be used to estimate which results can be expected. Null if it was not requested and non-null otherwise.

selectionCriterion.description: Null if this is a custom selection

confidenceExactMatch.description:
Confidence value that represents the certainty that reported consensus structure is exactly the measured one
 If multiple features support this consensus structure the maximum confidence is reported

confidenceApproxMatch.description:
Confidence value that represents the certainty that the exact consensus structure or a very similar
 structure (e.g. measured by Maximum Common Edge Subgraph Distance) is the measured one.
 If multiple features support this consensus structure the maximum confidence is reported

molecularFormula.description:
Molecular formula of the consensus annotation
 Might be null if no consensus formula is available.

supportingFeatureIds.description: FeatureIds where the topAnnotation supports this annotation.

selectionCriterion.description: Criterion that was used to select the consensus annotation.

molecularFormula.description:
Molecular formula of the consensus annotation
 Might be null if no consensus formula is available.

supportingFeatureIds.description: FeatureIds where the topAnnotation supports this annotation.

confidenceExactMatch.description: Confidence Score that represents the confidence whether the top hit is correct.

confidenceApproxMatch.description: Confidence Score that represents the confidence whether the top hit or a very similar hit (estimated by MCES distance) is correct.

expansiveSearchState.description: Result that shows if structure annotation was expanded by using PubChem as fallback and if so, which confidence mode was used (as per input parameter)

specifiedDatabases.description: List of databases that have been specified for structure db search. Null if no structure db search has been performed.

expandedDatabases.description: List of databases that have been used to expand search space during expansive search. Null if no structure db search has been performed.

FeatureAnnotations.description:
Summary of the results of a feature (aligned over runs). Can be added to a AlignedFeature.
 The different annotation fields within this summary object are null if the corresponding
 feature does not contain the represented results. If fields are non-null
 the corresponding result has been computed but might still be empty.

formulaId.description: Unique identifier of this formula candidate

molecularFormula.description: Molecular formula of this formula candidate.

siriusScoreNormalized.description:
Normalized Sirius Score of the formula candidate.
 If NULL result is not available

siriusScore.description:
Sirius Score (isotope + tree score) of the formula candidate.
 If NULL result is not available

zodiacScore.description:
Zodiac Score of the formula candidate.
 If NULL result is not available

predictedFingerprint.description: Probabilistic molecular fingerprint predicted by CSI:FingerID

FormulaCandidate.description:
Molecular formula candidate that holds a unique identifier (molecular formula + adduct).
 It can be extended with optional scoring metrics and the raw results
 such as fragmentation trees and simulated isotope pattern.

molecularFormula.description: neutral molecular formula of the fragment without adduct

adduct.description: This combines the ionization plus adduct of the fragment. In contrast to the FragmentationTree's adduct, this adduct may not include any in-source loss.

lipidSpecies.description:
Predicted lipid species in LIPID MAPS notation.
 NULL if not classified as lipid.

lipidMapsId.description: LIPID MAPS id of the predicted lipid class.

lipidClassName.description: Human-readable name of the predicted lipid class.

hypotheticalStructure.description:
Hypothetical molecular structure of the predicted lipid species as SMILES.
 NULL if hypothetical structure not available.

chainsUnknown.description: True if the formula composition of the chains could not be determined from the MS/MS.

MsData.description:
The MsData wraps all spectral input data belonging to a (aligned) feature. All spectra fields are optional. However, at least one Spectrum field needs to be set to create a valid MsData Object. The different types of spectra fields can be extended to adapt to other MassSpec measurement techniques not covered yet.

Each Feature can have: - One extracted isotope pattern (optional) - One merged MS/MS spectrum (optional) - One merged MS spectrum (optional) - many MS/MS spectra (optional) - many MS spectra (optional)

Each non-merged spectrum has an index which can be used to access the spectrum.

In the future we might add some additional information like chromatographic peak or something similar

parentIdx.description: Index to the parent peak connected by this loss in this particular spectrum

parentFragmentId.description:
Identifier of the parent fragment connected via this loss. Can be used to map fragments and peaks
 among fragmentation trees and spectra.

lossFormula.description: Molecular formula of the neutral loss that connects these two peaks.

ParentPeak.description: Link from annotated fragment peak to its parent fragment peak connected by their neutral loss.

fragmentId.description:
Identifier of the peak/fragment. Can be used to map fragments and peaks
 among fragmentation trees and spectra.

molecularFormula.description: Molecular formula that has been annotated to this peak

adduct.description: Adduct that has been annotated to this peak

exactMass.description: Exact mass of the annotated molecular formula and adduct

massDeviationMz.description: Absolute mass deviation of the exact mass to the measured peak mass in mDa

massDeviationPpm.description: Relative mass deviation of the exact mass to the measured peak mass in ppm

recalibratedMassDeviationMz.description: Absolute mass deviation of the exact mass to the recalibrated peak mass in mDa

recalibratedMassDeviationPpm.description: Relative mass deviation of the exact mass to the recalibrated peak mass in ppm

 (highlighted atoms)

substructureBondsCut.description:

 Array/List of indices of the bonds of the structure candidate that need to be cut to produce this fragments
 substructure (highlighted cut bonds).

 Null if substructure annotation not available or not requested.

 This score roughly reflects the probability of this fragment forming.

 This is the score of the path from root to this node which has the maximal score or "profit".
 The score of a path is equal to the sum of scores of its contained fragments and edges.
 Note: Refers to 'totalScore' in CombinatorialNode

 Null if substructure annotation not available or not requested.

hydrogenRearrangements.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: This field is experimental and may be changed (or even removed) without notice until it is declared stable.

 Number of hydrogens rearrangements needed to match the substructure to the fragment formula.

 Null if substructure annotation not available or not requested.

adduct.description: Adduct that has been annotated to this spectrum

Null if substructure annotation not available or not requested.

structureAnnotationSvg.description:

SVG graphics of the structure candidate used to derive substructure peak annotations via epimetheus insilico fragmentation Substructure highlighting (bond and atom indices) refers to this SVG.

Null if substructure annotation not available or not requested.

Overall score of all substructure annotations computed for this structure candidate (structureAnnotationSmiles)

Null if substructure annotation not available or not requested.

Specify the Phase I/Cyp450 mode for all provided BioTransformerSequenceSteps. Will only be applied to Steps that
 require the Cyp450 mode as parameter. Can be null in cases where only BioTransformerSequenceSteps are specified

 that do not need the Phase II mode.

Specify BioTransformerSequenceSteps to be applied to input structures. MultiStep MetabolicTransformations can
 only be used as singletons (list size of one).

AccountCredentials.description:
Simple object to hold account credentials, e.g. to perform login operations.
 If refreshToken is given, it is usually preferred over password based authentication.
 But in the end this is up to the respective web service.

name.description: Informative, human-readable name of this run

Name of the field to be used in search queries, e.g. ionMass:[300 TO 400]. Nested fields are addressed with dot notation. Dynamic, map-like fields are reported as concrete, directly usable field names - one entry per key currently present in the project index - rather than a wildcard template, e.g. tags.<tagName>, an element symbol in ...molecularFormula.<element>, or a database id in topAnnotations.matchedDatabases.<dbId>.

fullTextSearch.description:
If true, the field content is split into words and can be searched word by word (full text search).
 If false, TEXT fields only match as exact terms (though wildcards and regex are still possible).

sortable.description: If true, search results can be sorted by this field.

defaultSearchField.description: If true, this field is searched when a query term does not specify a field name.

possibleValues.description:
The values this field can take, exactly as they are indexed, or null if the field accepts free text.

Reported for ENUM and BOOLEAN fields, for TEXT fields that hold a closed vocabulary (the compound class ontologies), and for fields whose values are project state: a tag restricted by its definition, or the adducts detected in this project. Searchable fields are described per project, so the latter are the values actually present in it rather than everything that could ever occur.

Note that the indexed value is not always the notation you would expect: an adduct is indexed as '[M + H]+', with spaces. Use the values as offered rather than constructing them.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description of the field content, as shown in the API documentation.
 Plain text suitable for direct display (e.g. tooltips); deliberate paragraph breaks are newlines.

significantSuffixLength.description: How many trailing dot-separated segments of the field name carry its meaning, for compact display. 1 for a normal field (show the terminal segment, e.g. lipid); 2 for a dynamic map key (show field + key, e.g. matchedDatabases.GNPS, qualities.PEAK_QUALITY, tags.pfas); larger for multi-segment keys. Clients may show the last significantSuffixLength name segments as a short label; the full field name always stays authoritative for queries.

SearchableField.description:
Describes one field of the search index that can be used in lucene search queries (searchQuery parameter).
 Use this information to build valid queries, e.g. which fields support range queries ([300 TO 400])
 and which support word based (full text) search.

SearchableFieldType.description:
Value type of a searchable field. Determines which query clauses are valid for the field:
 TEXT supports terms, phrases, wildcards and regular expressions; numeric types (INTEGER, LONG, DOUBLE,
 FLOAT), DATE (yyyy-MM-dd) and TIME (HH\:mm\:ss) additionally support comparisons and range queries;
 BOOLEAN matches true/false; ENUM matches one of the possibleValues.

rowIds.description: Ids of the quantified objects, features or compounds depending on the row type.

Names of the runs the objects are quantified in, in the order of columnIds.

Optional field, only present if requested, since the table can be read by run id alone.

The name is the one the run carries in the project. It is either the sample name given when the data was imported, or, if none was given, derived from the measurement itself: the run id inside the file, and only failing that the file name. A name is therefore not necessarily the name of the file the run came from, and it is not guaranteed to be unique. Use columnSources to identify the input file, and columnIds to identify the run.

columnSources.description:
Files the runs were imported from, in the order of columnIds, to relate a column back to the input data. Same value as the source of the corresponding run.

Optional field, only present if requested, since it is not needed to read the table.

QuantTable.description: Quantification of features or compounds within the runs they have been detected in. Rows refer to the quantified objects, columns to the runs. Values that could not be quantified are NaN.

alignedFeatureId.description: Id of the feature (aligned over runs) this quality information belongs to.

categories.description:
Contains all pre-computation quality information that belong to
 this feature (aligned over runs), such as information about the quality of the peak shape, MS2 spectrum, etc.

Feature.description:
A feature as it has been detected in one single run, in contrast to an AlignedFeature which combines the features of the same compound over all runs it was detected in.

It provides the properties that are specific to the run it was detected in, such as its position on the retention time axis of that run and its quantity within that run.
